summary: No additional actionable runner defect established by this static review. The runner coherently centralizes spawning/signalling/reaping, retains its leader and admission slot during exceptional cleanup, separates EOF from EAGAIN, caps aggregate output, and serializes continuation completion. Two test defects remain in this frozen snapshot: stale-PID cleanup can signal unrelated processes, and inspection errors can falsely prove a descendant stopped. Coordinator has acknowledged both; corrections require a new snapshot.

findings.claim: P1 test safety defect: cleanUp reads historical PIDs from fixture files, checks isRunning and sends SIGKILL. After the runner releases ownership, either PID can be reused. The check-to-signal sequence also has a race, so a disposable worktree does not prevent signalling an unrelated host process.
findings.recommendation: Remove raw signalling of recorded numeric PIDs after ownership release. Use finite self-expiring fixture processes/output, or cleanup through a controller that still owns an unreaped anchor. A PID file or identity check followed by kill is not equivalent to retained ownership.

findings.claim: P2 test oracle defect: isRunning returns false for every short/failed proc_pidinfo result. Permission or inspection errors therefore satisfy assertions that descendants stopped. Its use for the direct child also does not itself prove reaping, although other tests use a stronger waitid oracle.
findings.recommendation: Treat only verified absence such as ESRCH as not running; surface other inspection failures as test failures. Keep the non-reaping waitid(P_PID,...WNOWAIT) ECHILD assertion for direct-child reaping. Apply it wherever a test claims the direct child was reaped.
